course: Earth and environmental science, with the measurement half of an introductory palaeoclimate course
curriculum: Why ice keeps a record at all: burial without melting
Accumulation rate, and what a site with little snow buys and costs
Firn: snow densifying into ice, and the close-off depth
Gas age against ice age, and why the difference matters
Annual layer counting, and where counting fails
Thinning with depth: flow, and where a record runs out
Depth–age scales, and putting two cores on one clock
Stable isotopes as a thermometer: δ¹⁸O and deuterium
Calibrating the isotope thermometer against instrumental temperature
Diffusion in firn, and the short events it erases
Resolution against record length — what choosing a site decides
What the trapped gas is, and what it is not
Carbon dioxide and methane records, and what a ppm is
Radiative forcing: turning a concentration into a temperature push
Volcanic sulphate horizons as dated tie points
Dust and tephra: aridity, wind and where the dust came from
Sea salt and the chemistry that reaches the ice
Cosmogenic ¹⁰Be, solar activity and geomagnetic markers
Radiometric dating and the decay law
What a proxy is: the chain between the thing and the number
Contamination and blanks in a cold laboratory
Drilling: fluid, brittle ice and what damage costs the record
Core logging, orientation and chain of custody
Replicate cores, and what agreement between them establishes
Random against systematic uncertainty
Separating a trend from year-to-year noise
Correlation between two records is not attribution
Splicing a proxy record onto the instrumental one
Model against data, and what a mismatch can mean
Reporting an uncertain record: what it licenses and what it does not
